Name: Missing User Interaction for Potentially Unsafe Action
Description:
The product encounters a situation in which some
         of its behavior is security-critical and should be authorized
         by a human before progressing, but it does not properly
         consult with the human user or its proxy (such as UI approval
         dialogues or pre-set policies) to determine whether it is
         allowed to perform the potentially dangerous
         behavior.

CommonConsequences.Note: This makes it easier for attackers to trick users into inflicting damage to their system.

References.Title: When the AI Edits Its Own Trust Boundary: Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in AWS's Agentic IDE

ObservedExamples.Description: Document editor runs macros without asking for user approval.
OS does not prompt the user to download and install ActiveX controls when the system is low on memory.
Chain: Web browser does not prompt the user before downloading an object that has an unrecognized content type (CWE-356), leading to untrusted search path (CWE-426) on a different OS.

AI agentic IDE product for cloud service does not consult the "Human-in-the-Loop" (HITL) in some security-critical decisions, allowing rewrite of its own Model Context Protocol (MCP), leading to configuration change and code execution [REF-1582].
AI agentic coding tool trusts a potentially-untrusted configuration input, causing it to skip a "trust confirmation dialog" before conducting potentially dangerous actions.
Chain: AI agentic coding tool auto-executes Yarn plugins in untrusted directories (CWE-696) before asking the user to approve the action (CWE-356).
Product does not warn user when document contains certain dangerous functions or macros.
Product does not warn user when document contains certain dangerous functions or macros.
Product does not warn user when document contains certain dangerous functions or macros.
Product does not warn user about a certificate if it has already been accepted for a different site. Possibly resultant.
File extractor does not warn user if setuid/setgid files could be extracted. Overlaps privileges/permissions.
Chain: E-mail client allows bypass of warning for dangerous attachments (CWE-356) via a Windows .LNK file that refers to the attachment (CWE-64).

AlternateTerms.Description: Used in various applications, especially for AI/ML applications, to indicate situations in which the human user must be consulted before determining the next action to take.

ModesOfIntroduction.Note: The architecture or design might include a component or potentially dangerous functionality that could effectively act independently.
A bug in the implementation could cause the product to fail to recognize that it is about to perform a dangerous operation requiring a human decision.

PotentialMitigations.Description: Product systems should warn users that a potentially dangerous action may occur if the user proceeds. For example, if the user downloads a file from an unknown source and attempts to execute the file on their machine, then the application's GUI can indicate that the file is unsafe.

Notes.Note: Often resultant, e.g. in unhandled error conditions.
Can overlap privilege errors, conceptually at least.
